market_context: United States/general English; refrigerated storage of cooked shrimp
title: How long does cooked shrimp last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long does cooked shrimp last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Cooked shrimp follows USDA cooked-seafood guidance: 3–4 days refrigerated at 40 °F or below when chilled within about two hours.
seo.search_intent: Learn how many days cooked shrimp keeps refrigerated and how to store leftovers safely.

excerpt: USDA says cooked fish and other seafood can be refrigerated for 3–4 days at 40 °F or below. Cooked shrimp should be chilled within about two hours after cooking or serving, and a normal smell does not extend that storage window.
content_html:
Cooking shrimp does not give it a week of refrigerator life. USDA's cooked-seafood guidance is 3–4 days at 40 °F/4 °C or below.

Count from the cooking day

Shrimp cooked on Monday should generally be used by Thursday or Friday if it was chilled promptly and kept cold.

Refrigerate within two hours

Cooked shrimp on a buffet or table should not remain unrefrigerated more than 2 hours, or one hour above 90 °F.

Smell does not reset the clock

Sour, rancid or ammonia-like odor is an obvious discard sign. Normal smell on day five, however, does not prove safety because pathogens may not cause noticeable spoilage.

Store in a covered shallow container

Shallow storage helps seafood cool quickly. Leaving shells on or removing them can change convenience and texture but does not extend the safety window.

Can cooked shrimp be frozen?

Yes. Frozen seafood remains safe while continuously held at 0 °F, although quality declines over time. Freezing leftover shrimp early generally preserves texture better than waiting several refrigerated days.

Bottom line

Use cooked shrimp within 3–4 refrigerator days. Chill promptly and freeze portions you will not use within that window.

faq.question: Can I eat cooked shrimp after five days?
faq.answer: USDA's conservative cooked-seafood window is 3–4 days, so discarding after five days is safer.

faq.question: Do shells make cooked shrimp last longer?
faq.answer: No. Shell-on versus peeled does not change the recommended safety window.

faq.question: What odor means shrimp is spoiled?
faq.answer: Sour, rancid or ammonia-like odor is a clear discard sign.
